240100101.text: This is a good idea... but can it really be done this way...?

240100103.text: Ah it's you! Thanks for your help previously with the photos! The sights they featured were truly inspiring.

240100104.text: I already have an approximate idea, and I've drawn up some drafts, but... Well, they're not up to snuff.

240100105.text: Don't misunderstand — this is not to say that I've painted some trash with no aesthetic value at all, but...

240100106.text: I feel that they're missing something special, something that can help them transcend the ordinary.

240100107.text: There's something too concrete about the things I have in mind... If I directly translated them into my painting, the beauty I wish to transmit will be damaged for sure.

240100108.text: *sigh* I fear this is a problem that every artist must face...

240100110.text: Thanks for the suggestion, but I fear that this problem will not be solved by a mere change of topics.

240100111.text: Whether it be mountains and rivers, birds and beasts, or the world of humanity... None of them can escape this issue.

240100112.text: It is precisely in their search for a solution that some of my colleagues have broken down and transmuted the sights they've seen using their inner feelings.

240100113.text: Such art emphasizes one's inner emotions most of all, and the result on the canvas is... How can I explain it...

240100114.text: Well, whether it be characters, scenery... Even light carries a sense of strangeness that no traditional sense of aesthetics can capture.

240100115.text: A simplistic glance would lead most to believe these paintings to be the brainchildren of the illiterate in art, or the mad.

240100116.text: But if you calm your spirit and get in tune with the artwork before you, you will hear it roar on the artist's behalf.

240100117.text: That roar comes from the artist's heart and soul, speaking their feelings aloud... and those feelings are, more often than not, rather intense.

240100118.text: Yet their voices cannot be perceived by the ear, but with the heart instead.

240100124.text: As for me... I do not yet wish to give in on the concrete, and so I've come up with another way.

240100125.text: I have decided to focus on color, and so I need to find stronger shades and simple yet powerful strokes.

240100126.text: At the same time, I need to weaken the lighting and traditional scene compositions... These things will affect my expression, and so I must ask them to temporarily leave the scene...

240100127.text: But the issue is that the strong, intense colors dictate the use of a lot of paint, and that I need to squeeze the paint directly onto the canvas to achieve the necessary effect.

240100128.text: So, I've... uh, run out of paint. However, I cannot simply move my easel away at the moment. That would surely affect my creative work...

240100129.text: Traveler, could I trouble you to visit Boucicaut? I've ordered a batch of good paints from him, and they should be ready at this point.

240100130.text: Or perhaps... Could you help me get some Whopperflower Nectar? That way, I could make a batch of paints on my own.

240100120.text: That's right. Some of my colleagues thought so too, and they are presently attempting to use some "figurative" methods of painting to produce something more abstract.

240100121.text: The most radical amongst them even wish to give up on depicting concrete objects altogether and simply use splotches of paint to express themselves... They call themselves "Neodescriptionists."

240100122.text: But I must say that even I cannot quite grasp their work. At most, I can only sense the rhythmic beauty contained within the colored splotches and line work...

240100123.text: As for what any given painting really expresses... I can only ask that painter to explain it to me.

240100201.text: Hello. What would you like to buy?

240100203.text: Oh, you're here to get paints for him? I've got them right here.

240100204.text: He really does use them up very quickly. You'd think he pours them straight into the water after buying them!

240100205.text: Well, regardless, here they are. Take them to him, would you?

240100401.text: Traveler, have you gotten the things I need? Hehe. Now then, did you bring paints, or Whopperflower nectar?

240100501.text: Thank you! These paints should last me for a while.

240100502.text: Don't spill them all into the water.

240100503.text: Into the water? Hahaha. I suppose my painting technique is just as you describe.

240100504.text: But only by squeezing the paint out and directly pouring it out onto the canvas before using a carving blade and palette knife will provide me with the touch necessary to make an impact on others.

240100505.text: Thanks for your help. I should be able to continue with the aid of these paints. Come over and take a look when you have the time, alright?

240100506.text: It is all thanks to your help that my work has started out on the right foot, after all.

240100507.text: Once this painting is complete, I hope that you'll be the first to come appreciate it.

240100601.text: This nectar is not bad! Very good — great paint shall surely come of this.

240100602.text: What sort of paints do you want to make?

240100603.text: Hmm... I'd like to make ones that lean towards warm shades, but with a melancholy touch.

240100604.text: They'll also need to be thick enough to allow me to work with compact brushstrokes.

240100301.text: We cannot be too restricted by concrete forms... We must draw the beauty out and use symbolic methods too...

240100302.text: No, no... Still no. This composition is too deliberate...
